title: rwb-access treatment and plan-timer slice: the authorise request and answer, the Treatment and offer and Case record letters and the rwb-access login are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.2, T6.1 and T6.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4, A2.7 and A2.14; Legacy RWB-E2-004 sections 10 and 12
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 to 7; section 10 Authority; section 11 Data; section 12.1 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Three values this slice needs are absent from the sources. (1) Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 name POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) the first API path of rwb-access, but the TSD P4 appendix T-A endpoint inventory has no authorise path and no request or answer schema, so the fields the caller sends (identity, capability area, right, treatment reference, case reference, the case attributes for the scope test, the field IDs, and for an approval the approval level, the decision code, the regulation item, the product group and the amounts) and the fields the answer returns (decision code, matrix version, masking answer per field ID, scope result, entry reference, and for an approval the level, the delegation row, the limit version and the outcome) are a design read, not a source value. (2) The TSD P4 T6.1 RBAC matrix tabulates only three capability areas (Rules and parameters, Reference data, Platform administration), so the TREATMENT_AND_OFFER and CASE_RECORD letters of RW-RESTRUCT, RW-CASEOWN, RW-PHONECOL and the other recovery roles are not tabulated anywhere; the letters are read from the policy pack as data. (3) The per-service login name is named by DP-02 and by no document.
evidence: TSD P4 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none is /authorise or /doa-limits; T6.1 has three columns only; Architecture v5 slide 14 gives the call and its tags, not its fields; FSD P4 A2.4 gives VR-P4-004-1 and MSG-P4-002 but no field list
proposed: Freeze the authorise and doa-limits request and answer in RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-P4-E2004-APP at contract review; load the two capability areas into the policy pack as rows (RWB-P4-AD002-APP); name the login with the platform DB story of DP-02

title: The delegation lookup GET /doa-limits and its request and answer fields exist only on Architecture v5 slide 14, not in the TSD P4 appendix
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (P4 IN: GET /doa-limits) and slide 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD P4 A2.6
section: Section 4 Flow steps 8 to 10; section 7 AC4 and AC5; section 12.1 Contract; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 13 Build steps 6 and 7
description: Architecture v5 slide 14 lists GET /doa-limits among the operations rwb-access accepts, and slide 41 gives /authorise as the service's first API path. The TSD P4 appendix T-A has neither path: API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 are the list, reference-load, role, access-log, session, break-glass, rule-package and smoke operations, and no delegation read is among them. The request fields this slice needs (decisionCode, regulationItem, productGroup, principal, lossPct, lossAmount, onDate) and the answer fields (level, delegationLimitId, limitVersion, holderUserId, substituteUserId, outcome) are therefore a design read from the FSD A2.6 lookup AC and from the delegation_limit column set of TSD P4 T3.1, not a source value. The outcome value set (COVERED, NOT_COVERED, NO_HOLDER, NO_AMOUNT_LIMIT, RELATED_PARTY) is likewise not tabulated. R-PREC puts Architecture v5 first, so this story's contract corrects the TSD appendix rather than the other way round.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 P4 IN line names GET /doa-limits; TSD P4 T-A.1 has 18 endpoints and none is a DoA read; FSD P4 AC-ALT-P4-006-01 and AC-EXC-P4-006-04 give the answers but no field names
proposed: Add API-P4-022 GET /doa-limits to the P4 API specification with the request and answer of this story's section 12.1, and keep the outcome value set in the page of the contract; RWB-P4-E2013-APP consumes the same operation

title: Which delegation limit version is in force on the approval date of a treatment is a data state, not a document value
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.6 AC-P4-006-01 and AC-ALT-P4-006-02; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (delegation_limit valid_from, valid_to, limit_version); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 6 notes
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 8 and 9; section 9 State transitions; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The documents name DOA-2026.11 as the version in force from 30 November 2026 and DOA-2027.01 as the version that replaces it from 1 January 2027, and the FSD change AC shows a lookup moving from L6 to L5 across that boundary. They do not fix which version is in force in SIT, UAT or production on the date a given treatment is approved, because the version in force is a property of the loaded rows and their valid_from and valid_to, and the environments are loaded at different times. A story that read the label DOA-2026.11 as if it were the answer would answer a level against a version that may not be in force on the approval date it is asked about. This slice therefore reads the version from the row window on the date asked, and the version in force per environment stays a data question for the DoA load story.
evidence: FSD P4 A2.6 AC-P4-006-01 names DOA-2026.11 with 95 limits and 218 rows; AC-ALT-P4-006-02 names DOA-2027.01 from 2027-01-01; TSD P4 T3.1 has valid_from, valid_to and limit_version on delegation_limit; no document names the version in force per environment
proposed: Decide the version in force per environment at the DoA load (RWB-P4-E1038-APP) and keep it out of code; the lookup always answers the version whose window covers the date asked, and the answer names it

title: The composite route field list for SCR-14 Treatment record and the SCR-03 timer panel is not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 (gateway-bff merges rwb-case and rwb-source-data) and slide 14; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 Screens; Legacy RWB-E2-004 section 15
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 12.1 Contract; section 15 Screens and states
description: DP-19 sends both screens through the gateway-bff composite route, and slide 10 fixes only the pattern: the gateway asks each owner directly, in parallel, one hop each, and merges the answers into the screen model. No document lists the fields SCR-14 shows of a treatment or the fields the SCR-03 timer panel shows, so the field IDs that this story's decision must carry (the treatment record fields DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-014 and DF-TRT-029, and the timer fields DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 and DF-WRK-042) are a design read. The story answers this by accepting the field IDs in the request rather than fixing them in code, so the route can name whatever it shows.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 10 notes describe the merge and the response budget, not the fields; FSD P4 Screens lists SCR-41 and SCR-43 for the DoA and the roles, not SCR-14 or SCR-03; the legacy story's section 15 names the screens and no field list
proposed: Publish the two composite routes with their field lists in the gateway-bff route catalogue and confirm that no field on either is a personal field; the masking proof of this story then covers the published list

title: The per-service login of rwb-access is named by DP-02 and by no document
source: Template and Rules v1 section R4 (login per service) and R5.5 DP-02; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T1; Architecture v5 slide 41 notes
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 10 Authority; section 13 Database and migrations
description: Architecture v5 slide 41 says every service has its own login in the ACE database and DP-02 turns that into one login per service, but no document gives the login name of rwb-access, its grants or the role that owns its schema objects. The name is needed by the migration, the connection pool and the test container of this story, and it cannot be derived from the service name by a rule the sources state.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 notes: schema rwb_<name> with its own login; slide 14 P4 DB line; TSD P4 T1 says one service, one repository, one front end and names no login; DP-02 adds no name
proposed: Fix the login name, its grants and its schema owner in the platform DB story of DP-02, and reference it from every P4 story rather than repeating it
